egen

Repeat the first nonmissing value

Stata 

egen z = firstnm(x)

R base 

data$z <- data$x[which(!is.na(data$x))[1]]

Stata reference · R reference

Repeat the interquartile range

Stata 

egen z = iqr(x)

R base 

data$z <- diff(stats::quantile(data$x,c(.25,.75),na.rm=TRUE,type=2))

Differs from Stata Uses R quantile type 2 for Stata's default empirical percentile rule.

Express values as percentages of the column total

Stata 

egen z = pc(x)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = tidystata::pc(x))

Computes 100 * x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), not percentile ranks. Use prop = TRUE for shares summing to 1; use dplyr::percent_rank() for percentile ranks. The observed total must be finite and nonzero.

Stata reference · R reference

Calculate percentile ranks (percent rank) on a 0-1 scale

Stata 

tempvar x_rank x_n
egen `x_rank' = rank(x), track
egen `x_n' = count(x)
generate p = (`x_rank' - 1) / (`x_n' - 1) if !missing(x)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, p = dplyr::percent_rank(x))

Uses (minimum rank - 1) / (nonmissing count - 1). Ties receive the lowest rank; missing values stay missing. For c(2, 3, 5), returns c(0, 0.5, 1). With tied maxima the top rank can be below 1; a single observed value has an undefined rank. This differs from cumulative proportions computed by cume_dist() or stats::ecdf().

Stata reference · R reference

Calculate percentile ranks (percent rank) on a 0-100 scale

Stata 

tempvar x_rank x_n
egen `x_rank' = rank(x), track
egen `x_n' = count(x)
generate p = 100 * (`x_rank' - 1) / (`x_n' - 1) if !missing(x)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, p = 100 * dplyr::percent_rank(x))

Uses (minimum rank - 1) / (nonmissing count - 1) * 100. Ties receive the lowest rank; missing values stay missing. For c(2, 3, 5), returns c(0, 50, 100). With tied maxima the top rank can be below 100; a single observed value has an undefined rank. This differs from cumulative proportions computed by cume_dist() or stats::ecdf().

expandcl

Duplicate whole groups with fresh group identifiers

Stata 

expandcl 2, cluster(g) generate(newg)

R base 

parts <- split(data,data$g); data <- do.call(rbind,lapply(seq_along(parts),function(k) do.call(rbind,lapply(1:2,function(j) transform(parts[[k]],newg=(k-1L)*2L+j)))))

Differs from Stata Validates cluster membership and copy counts; the numeric assignment/order of new IDs may differ from Stata.

fmerge

Perform a validated ftools-style one-to-one merge

Stata 

fmerge 1:1 id using other.dta, nogenerate

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::full_join(data,other,by='id',relationship='one-to-one')

Requires disjoint non-key column names unless update is explicitly shown. dplyr suffixes overlapping names; ordinary Stata merge preserves master values, including master missing values, on matched rows.

fralias

Read linked values dynamically without storing a copied column

Stata 

fralias add score, from(link)

R base 

get_score <- function() lookup$score[match(data$id,lookup$id)]

R accessor-function workflow, not an alias column: call get_score() each time; modifications belong in lookup.

frget

Rename a linked value when copying it

Stata 

frget newscore=score, from(link)

R base 

data$newscore <- lookup$score[data$link]

Value-copy workflow; frame linkage and Stata metadata are not carried into R.

Copy a value through an established table link

Stata 

frget score, from(link)

R base 

data$score <- lookup$score[data$link]

frlink

Validate and construct a one-to-one table link

Stata 

frlink 1:1 id, frame(lookup)

R base 

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data$id),!anyDuplicated(lookup$id)); link <- match(data$id,lookup$id)

link is a fixed R object name; unmatched keys produce NA. Rebuild after source changes.

Stata reference · R reference

Build a many-to-one row link to a lookup table

Stata 

frlink m:1 id, frame(lookup) generate(link)

R base 

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(lookup$id)); data$link <- match(data$id,lookup$id)

R match indices are a snapshot and must be rebuilt after lookup row reordering.

Stata reference · R reference

frunalias

Materialize a dynamically looked-up value as a column

Stata 

frunalias score

R base 

data$score <- lookup$score[match(data$id, lookup$id)]

Materialize an ordinary R column snapshot. Requires data and lookup tables with matching id keys and a lookup score column; later lookup changes do not change this column.
